extracted.intended_audience: Veterans, service members, family members, community providers, stakeholders, and VA staff who wish to submit comments on VA Federal Register proposed rules and notices
extracted.subtask_short: submitting comments to VA Federal Register
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for submitting public comments on VA proposed rules and Federal Register documents (via Regulations.gov or addresses in the Federal Register), plus content guidance on what makes effective VA comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on rules, proposed rules, and notices should be submitted through Regulations.gov, to agency dockets on Regulations.gov, or to other places identified under the 'Addresses' heading in Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Federal Register 'Addresses' heading for any alternate submission routes. The guide provides visual instructions for submitting comments both as an individual and as an organization; to leave a comment click the comment button which directs you to the document open for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-by-step process for leaving a comment
rubrics_metrics.description: To leave a comment, click the comment button. You will be directed to a document open for comment and can click the comment button to leave a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the on-screen comment form on Regulations.gov; the VA guide includes visual aids for both individual and organizational submitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: National standards of practice are typically available for comment for 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the specific Federal Register notice for the exact opening and closing dates; 60 days is the typical duration for national standards of practice but individual notices may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: VA employee commenting restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: VA employees should not comment via the Federal Register. If you are a VA employee and would like to comment, navigate to the National Standards of Practice Employee Participation and Review site page via VA SharePoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA employee comments made via Regulations.gov will be withdrawn. Use the internal SharePoint process instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save your Comment Tracking Number
rubrics_metrics.description: You can save your Comment Tracking Number for future reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save it by printing the webpage and emailing the number to yourself, or by clicking the email opt-in button on the comment form prior to finalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify yourself
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly stating your status (veteran, service member, family member, provider) helps contextualize your perspective and the weight of your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specific service-connected conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference specific service-connected conditions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, tie your comment to precise conditions to illustrate direct impacts or concerns linked to the proposed change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific 38 CFR provisions being amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific 38 CFR provisions being amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointing to exact regulatory citations clarifies which rules your comment addresses and helps reviewers locate and evaluate your input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with program impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with veterans' health, benefit, or burial program impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the proposed rule would affect program delivery, access, quality, or eligibility for veterans and beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data on veteran population impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data on veteran population impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with quantitative or qualitative data about affected veteran populations where possible to strengthen the comment's persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference VA Office of Inspector General (OIG) reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference VA's Office of Inspector General reports where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite OIG findings to support claims about program weaknesses, risks, or prior recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite GAO and CRS reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite GAO and CRS reports on VA programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Government Accountability Office (GAO) and Congressional Research Service (CRS) analyses to substantiate broader policy or program-level points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Choice/MISSION Act implementation considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, discuss how the proposed rule interacts with or affects implementation of Choice, MISSION Act, or related access-to-care policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide community provider perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide community provider perspective if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community (non-VA) providers should explain practical impacts on their ability to deliver services to veterans, including operational, credentialing, or reimbursement considerations.
